artifacts.summary: Built Stage 3.5 Dispatch Prep in skill-orchestrate (memory retrieval + --lit resolution), threaded --clean/--fast end to end, fixed the multi-task description gap, and wired all 10 dispatch sites.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added a single shared Stage 3.5 Dispatch Prep procedure to skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md providing memory retrieval and --lit literature-briefing resolution, threaded --clean/--fast through orchestrate.md and the skill's Stage 1/1b/MT-1, fixed the pre-existing multi-task description gap, and wired all 7 single-task dispatch sites and 3 multi-task dispatch loops to inject the new stage's outputs into their prompts.

memory_candidates.content: When editing a large prose/pseudo-code SKILL.md file with many structurally-identical dispatch-site blocks (same bash snippet, same table shape, differing only in preceding heading text), disambiguate Edit tool old_string matches by including the following unique heading (e.g. the next `#### State:` line) as trailing context in old_string, rather than trying to make the preceding text unique. This lets each Edit call target one occurrence precisely even when 5+ near-identical blocks exist in the same file.

Before wiring a shared procedure into every 'Agent-dispatch site' named in a plan's audit phase, distinguish lifecycle dispatch sites (Stage 4/MT-4 style: research/plan/implement, writes a real handoff) from narrow helper dispatches (drift-inspection forks, blocker-escalation forks/revisers) that share the same 'Invoke the Agent tool:' surface syntax but serve a different, single purpose with a different orchestrator_mode. A plan's explicitly repeated closed count (e.g. '7+3=10') is a strong signal that helper dispatches are deliberately out of scope, not an oversight to fix silently.
